blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Learned feature representations in neural networks often contain structure beyond that directly used by the final task output.
We study this structure using passive probes that apply fixed, untrained,
property-independent projections to representations as they evolve during training.
We motivate this approach through the task of prediction on 𝒮 2 \mathcal{S}^{2} where
equivalent vector and Hermitian parameterizations reveal an additional loss-invariant trace coordinate.
This motivates a general construction in which fixed random projections serve as
observers of learned features.
Because the observer is loss-invariant and independent of the property being studied, changes in accessibility reflect changes in the representation relative to
the fixed observer rather than adaptation of the observer itself.
We show that ensembles of passive probes can directly reflect task-relevant
information such as target alignment.
Under our constructions, the accessibility of eventual difficulty evolves
differently across tasks.
It increases during training in the regression tasks of surface-normal estimation
and image inpainting but remains near its initial level in image classification.
Comparisons with learned linear probes further show that recoverability and
passive accessibility can evolve differently during training.
Together, these results show how passive probes can separately characterize changes in representation geometry and the accessibility of eventual task difficulty.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Learned representations are commonly analyzed by asking what properties can be
recovered from them or how their geometry changes across layers, models, or
training. A standard approach to the first question is probing where an
auxiliary predictor is trained on a frozen representation to recover a property
of interest ( Alain and Bengio, 2017 ; Conneau et al., 2018 ) .
Linear evaluation of frozen features is likewise widely used to evaluate
learned visual representations ( Chen et al., 2020 ) . These approaches
provide useful measures of recoverability , which indicates whether an observer adapted to the representation can extract a target property from it.

blocks.en:
The interpretation of probe performance, however, depends partly on how the
observer is fitted. Probe capacity can allow memorization that obscures
what can be attributed to the representation ( Hewitt and Liang, 2019 ) , while alternative formulations emphasize sample efficiency, description length, and the inductive bias provided by a representation ( Voita and Titov, 2020 ; Immer et al., 2022 ) .
More broadly, different probing methodologies address different questions about a representation ( Belinkov, 2022 ) .
These observations do not make learned probes unsuitable but clarify that
probe performance reflects both the representation and the observer fitted
to the property of interest.

blocks.en:
A complementary line of work compares representations through their geometry.
Representational similarity analysis compares patterns of pairwise dissimilarity ( Kriegeskorte et al., 2008 ) , while methods based on canonical correlation analysis, such as SVCCA ( Raghu et al., 2017 ) , compare representations under transformations of their feature coordinates.
Centered kernel alignment (CKA) provides a related similarity measure with specified invariances and has proved effective for comparing neural representations across networks and initializations ( Kornblith et al., 2019 ) . Such methods characterize important aspects of representation geometry, but do not ask what becomes accessible to an observer that itself remains unchanged during learning.
More generally, different representational similarity measures encode different notions of equivalence and can differ in their sensitivity to changes in the underlying representation ( Williams et al., 2021 ; Ding et al., 2021 ) .
Such methods characterize important aspects of representation geometry, but
do not ask what becomes accessible to an observer that itself remains
unchanged during learning.

This leaves a complementary observational question: what becomes accessible to a fixed observer as the representation changes
during learning? We study this question using passive probes which are loss-invariant, scalar projections sampled independently of the property of interest and held fixed across the training trajectory. Unlike a learned probe, a passive probe is not optimized to recover the target.
Consequently, changes in its relationship to that target reflect changes in the
representation relative to the fixed observer rather than adaptation of the observer.
We refer to this quantity as passive accessibility , distinguishing it from recoverability after fitting a learned probe.

We additionally introduce a strict construction that removes the row space of
the final task readout from the passive direction (see Figure 1 ).
Null-space projections have previously been used to remove linearly recoverable properties from representations and to study their behavioral relevance ( Ravfogel et al., 2020 ; Elazar et al., 2021 ) .
The role of the null space here is different as we do not learn a direction from the property and then remove it.
Instead, the passive direction is property-independent and is projected into the null space of the task readout . The resulting scalar coordinate is therefore task-readout-invariant. When the loss depends only on that readout, it is also loss-invariant.

blocks.en: 4 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 4 结论

blocks.en:
Passive probes provide a framework for examining how task-relevant information becomes accessible during learning without explicit fitting of the probe to the property of interest.
Their relationship to representation geometry supports the interpretation of these measurements, including probing the null space of the final task output. Across the three tasks considered, the findings reveal different levels of accessibility of eventual difficulty from its fixed, untrained directions.
The contrasting behavior of classification and the two regression tasks indicates that this relationship depends on the learning setting.
Passive probes differ in information content from learned probes and can thus provide complementary evidence about the organization of learned representations.
Further work is needed to establish how the task, training objective, and architecture contribute to the observed differences.

被动探测器提供了一个框架,用以审查在学习过程中如何获得与任务有关的信息,而无需将探测器明确适用于感兴趣的财产。
它们与表示几何的关系支持对这些测量的解释,包括检测最终任务输出的空地. 在所审议的三项任务中,调查结果显示,最终难以从固定的、未经培训的方向获得服务的程度不同。
分类的对比行为和两个回归任务表明这种关系取决于学习环境.
被动探针在信息内容上与所学探针不同,因此可以为所学探针的组织提供补充证据.
需要进一步努力确定任务、培训目标和结构如何促进观察到的差异。

In this work, we used generative AI tools to assist in critically evaluating and refining an author-developed conceptual framework and mathematical derivations, checking mathematical claims, refining hypotheses, designing aspects of the experimental and analysis methodology, implementing and debugging analysis code, and interpreting experimental results.
The core research idea, including the initial identification of the loss-invariant degree of freedom, the relevant equivalence, and the foundational mathematical formulation motivating this work, was developed by the authors.
Generative AI was subsequently used to stress-test these ideas, explore their implications and generalizations, identify potential confounds and controls, and assist in developing and validating the resulting experimental analysis.
blocks.zh:
在这项工作中,我们使用基因AI工具协助批判性地评价和完善作者制定的概念框架和数学推论,检查数学索赔,完善假设,设计实验和分析方法的各个方面,实施并调试分析代码,并解释实验结果.
核心研究思想由作者提出,包括初步确定自由程度的丧失-变化、相关等同性以及推动这项工作的基础数学公式。
基因AI后来被用来测试这些想法的压力,探索其影响和概括,确定潜在的混乱和被控制,并协助发展和验证由此产生的实验分析.

blocks.en: We did not use generative AI tools to generate or modify the experimental datasets or to fabricate, alter, or selectively choose experimental measurements. Tasks involving translation, qualitative or thematic data analysis, and human-subject research were not applicable to this work.
blocks.zh: 我们没有使用基因AI工具来生成或修改实验数据集,也没有编织,篡改或有选择地选择实验测量. 涉及翻译、定性或专题数据分析和人的研究的任务不适用于这项工作。

blocks.en: Additionally, we used generative AI tools for brainstorming, literature search and synthesis, critical assessment of novelty and positioning, software development and debugging, organization of the manuscript, and drafting and editing scientific text for clarity.
blocks.zh: 此外,我们使用基因化的AI工具进行集思广益、文献搜索和综合、对新颖性和定位的批判性评估、软件开发和调试、手稿的组织、以及科学文本的起草和编辑以明确。

blocks.en:
All AI-assisted research contributions were reviewed and validated by the authors. Mathematical statements and derivations used in the work were checked by the authors against their definitions and where applicable verified numerically.
AI-assisted experimental and analysis code was tested using analytic or synthetic sanity checks, endpoint identities, independent replay of saved checkpoints, and numerical comparison against previously saved experimental outputs.
Experimental conclusions were based on results produced by the implemented experiments rather than on generative-AI predictions
Literature and novelty claims arising during AI-assisted discussion were checked against the cited literature.
The authors made the final decisions regarding the mathematical formulation, hypotheses, experimental design, interpretation, claims, and manuscript content.
